It solves the problem of identifying cells both spatially and hierarchically within a dense or sparse octree structure, enabling efficient neighbor and parent lookups [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method solves the problem of identifying cells spatially and hierarchically within an octree, enabling efficient neighbor and parent lookups. Source [S1] explicitly states in section 3.4.2 that Morton coding is used 'to identify our cells spatially and hierarchically within our octree structure.' It further details that the root key is 1, child keys are formed by concatenating the parent's key with the 3-bit binary representation of the octant index, and each level adds 3 bits. It also mentions that parent keys can be found via a bit shift operation (implying efficient lookup). The notes provided in the prompt align perfectly with the Portuguese text in [S1], confirming the facts about spatial/hierarchical identification, the root key of 1, the concatenation method, the 3-bit increment, and the capability for efficient lookups.
